lanes.label: The return and the new creation
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Revelation: overview
nodes.d: Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ given to John on Patmos: letters to seven churches, a vision of the throne in heaven, the Lamb, series of seals, trumpets and bowls, and the end in the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the main parts of Revelation as the book itself presents them?
ev: Say who gave the revelation and to whom
Name the main parts: churches, throne, Lamb, judgments, new heaven and earth
Say what is promised to the one who reads and keeps it in 1:3

nodes.t: Prologue: the revelation of Jesus Christ
nodes.d: John introduces the revelation Jesus Christ gave, blesses those who read, hear and keep it, greets the seven churches from the God who is, was and is to come and from Jesus Christ, and announces that he cometh with clouds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Revelation introduces itself and who Jesus is in these verses?
ev: Say who is the source of the revelation in 1:1
Name what Jesus is called in 1:5
Describe what 1:7 says about his coming

nodes.t: John's vision of Christ among the lampstands
nodes.d: John on Patmos hears a voice and sees one like the Son of man among seven golden candlesticks, with eyes like fire and a two-edged sword from his mouth, who says he is first and last, alive for evermore, holding the keys of death and hell.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vision of Christ in Revelation 1 and what he says to John?
ev: Describe what John saw
Say what Christ says about himself in 1:17-18
Say what the seven stars and seven candlesticks are in 1:20

nodes.t: Letter to Ephesus: leaving the first love
nodes.d: Christ commends Ephesus for works, patience and testing false apostles, but says they have left their first love and must repent; to the one who overcomes he promises the tree of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ praises and corrects in the church at Ephesus?
ev: Say what Christ commends and what he has against Ephesus
State the promise to the one who overcomes

nodes.t: Letter to Smyrna: faithful unto death
nodes.d: Christ, who was dead and is alive, tells poor but rich Smyrna not to fear coming suffering, to be faithful unto death, and promises the crown of life and no hurt from the second death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ promises to the faithful at Smyrna?
ev: Say what Christ says not to fear
State the promise in 2:10-11

nodes.t: Letter to Pergamos: holding fast, yet holding false teaching
nodes.d: Christ commends Pergamos for holding his name even where Satan dwells and where Antipas was killed, but rebukes them for holding the teaching of Balaam and of the Nicolaitanes, and calls them to repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ commends and rebukes at Pergamos?
ev: Say what Pergamos did well
Name the wrong teachings Christ names
State the promise in 2:17

nodes.t: Letter to Thyatira: Jezebel and holding fast
nodes.d: Christ commends Thyatira's love, service, faith and patience, rebukes them for tolerating Jezebel who teaches fornication and idol food, and tells the rest to hold fast until he comes, promising power over nations and the morning star.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Christ says about Jezebel and about those who did not follow her?
ev: Say what Christ commends in 2:19
Describe the charge in 2:20
State the promise in 2:26-28

nodes.t: Letter to Sardis: a name that thou livest, and art dead
nodes.d: Christ tells Sardis that they have a name for being alive but are dead, calls them to watch and repent, notes a few who have not defiled their garments, and promises white raiment and his confession of the name of the one who overcomes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Christ says to the church at Sardis and what he promises to the few?
ev: Say what Christ says about Sardis' reputation
Describe the promise in 3:4-5

nodes.t: Letter to Philadelphia: the open door
nodes.d: Christ, holy and true, holding the key of David, tells Philadelphia he has set before them an open door, they kept his word, he will keep them from the hour of temptation, and the overcomer will be a pillar in his temple with the name of the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ commends and promises to the church at Philadelphia?
ev: Describe what Christ has set before Philadelphia
State the promise to the one who overcomes in 3:12

nodes.t: Letter to Laodicea: lukewarm, and Christ at the door
nodes.d: Christ rebukes Laodicea for being neither cold nor hot and for saying they are rich while they are wretched, counsels them to buy gold, white raiment and eyesalve from him, and says he stands at the door and knocks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Christ says to Laodicea and the invitation in 3:20?
ev: Describe what Laodicea thinks of itself and what Christ says they are
Explain the picture in 3:20
State the promise to the overcomer in 3:21

nodes.t: The throne in heaven
nodes.d: John is called up through an open door and sees a throne with one sitting on it, a rainbow, twenty-four elders in white with crowns, four living creatures crying holy, holy, holy, and all worship God as Creator.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the throne room scene and what the worshippers say?
ev: Describe what surrounds the throne
Say what the four beasts and the elders say and do
Say why God is worthy according to 4:11

nodes.t: The sealed scroll and the Lamb
nodes.d: John weeps that no one can open the sealed scroll until the Lion of the tribe of Juda appears as a Lamb as though slain, takes the scroll, and heaven and every creature worship him as worthy because he redeemed people from every nation by his blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is worthy to open the scroll and why?
ev: Say why John wept and what was announced
Describe the Lamb and what he does
Say what the new song says about why he is worthy

nodes.t: The first six seals
nodes.d: The Lamb opens six seals: four horsemen, the souls under the altar crying how long, and a great earthquake with the sun black and the moon as blood, so that people hide from the wrath of the Lamb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the six seals in order as John sees them?
ev: List the four horses and what each rider holds or does
Describe the cry of the souls under the altar and the answer they receive
Say how the people respond to the sixth seal

nodes.t: The sealed servants and the great multitude
nodes.d: Before the winds are released, 144,000 servants from the tribes of Israel are sealed, and John then sees a countless multitude from all nations in white robes before the throne and the Lamb, who came out of great tribulation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two groups in Revelation 7 and what the text says about the multitude?
ev: Describe the sealing in 7:1-8
Say who the great multitude is according to 7:13-14
State what God and the Lamb do for them in 7:15-17

nodes.t: The seventh seal and the first four trumpets
nodes.d: The seventh seal brings silence in heaven, seven angels receive trumpets, an angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, and the first four trumpets strike a third of the earth, sea, rivers and lights, ending with a cry of woe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the first four trumpets as they are given in chapter 8?
ev: Say what happens at the seventh seal
Describe what the first four trumpets strike
Say what the flying angel announces in 8:13

nodes.t: The fifth and sixth trumpets
nodes.d: At the fifth trumpet the bottomless pit is opened and locusts torment people who lack the seal of God, and at the sixth four angels at the Euphrates are loosed with a great army, yet the rest do not repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happens at the fifth and sixth trumpets and how people respond?
ev: Describe the fifth trumpet and who is harmed
Say what the sixth trumpet looses
Say what the surviving people fail to do in 9:20-21

nodes.t: The mighty angel and the little book
nodes.d: A mighty angel stands on sea and land and swears by the Creator that there will be no more delay, and John is told to take and eat the little book, sweet in his mouth and bitter in his belly, and to prophesy again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what John is told and shown in Revelation 10?
ev: Describe the angel and what he swears
Say what John does with the little book
Say what John is told to do afterward

nodes.t: The temple measured and the two witnesses
nodes.d: John is told to measure the temple while the court is given to the Gentiles, and two witnesses prophesy in sackcloth, are killed by the beast from the pit, lie in the great city three and a half days, and are raised and called up to heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the two witnesses do and what happens to them in Revelation 11?
ev: Describe what John is told to measure and not measure
Describe the two witnesses and what happens to them
Say how the survivors respond in 11:13

nodes.t: The seventh trumpet: the kingdoms become the Lord's
nodes.d: At the seventh trumpet loud voices in heaven say the kingdoms of this world have become those of the Lord and his Christ, the elders worship, and the temple in heaven opens to show the ark of his testament.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what is announced when the seventh angel sounds?
ev: Say what the voices announce in 11:15
Say what the elders thank God for in 11:17-18
Describe what is seen in the temple in 11:19

nodes.t: The woman, the dragon and the man child
nodes.d: John sees a woman clothed with the sun who bears a man child who is caught up to God, a great red dragon who tries to devour the child, war in heaven in which the dragon is cast down, and the dragon's pursuit of the woman and her seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the main figures of Revelation 12 and what the text says each does?
ev: Describe the woman, the dragon and the child
Say who the dragon is named in 12:9
Say how the saints overcome him in 12:11
Describe what the dragon does after he is cast down

nodes.t: The beast from the sea and the beast from the earth
nodes.d: John sees a beast rise out of the sea receiving authority from the dragon and making war on the saints, and a second beast from the earth that makes people worship the first, speaks as a dragon, and imposes a mark and the number 666.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe both beasts in Revelation 13 and what they cause people to do?
ev: Describe the first beast and what it is given
Describe what the second beast does
Say whose names are not written in the book of life in 13:8

nodes.t: The Lamb on Zion, three angels and the harvest
nodes.d: John sees the Lamb on mount Sion with 144,000 redeemed, three angels announcing the everlasting gospel, Babylon's fall and a warning about the beast's mark, a blessing on the dead in the Lord, and the harvest and winepress of God's wrath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the sights and the three angels' messages in Revelation 14?
ev: Describe the 144,000 and their song
List the messages of the three angels
Describe the two images of harvest and winepress

nodes.t: The song of Moses and the Lamb; seven angels with bowls
nodes.d: John sees seven angels with the seven last plagues and those who conquered the beast singing the song of Moses and of the Lamb on a sea of glass, after which the angels receive golden bowls of God's wrath and the temple fills with smoke.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the scene before the seven bowls are poured out?
ev: Say who sings and what they sing about
Describe what the seven angels are given

nodes.t: The seven bowls of wrath
nodes.d: The seven angels pour out bowls on the earth, sea, rivers, sun, the beast's throne, Euphrates and air, with a call to watch, gathering at Armageddon, a great earthquake and Babylon remembered before God, while people curse God and do not repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the seven bowls and how people respond?
ev: List what each of the seven bowls is poured on
Say what the angel of the waters says about God in 16:5-7
Say how people respond in 16:9, 11 and 21

nodes.t: The woman on the scarlet beast
nodes.d: An angel shows John the judgment of the great whore, Babylon the great, seated on a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns and drunk with the blood of the saints; the angel explains the mystery and says the Lamb will overcome the beast's allies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what John sees in Revelation 17 and what the angel explains?
ev: Describe the woman and the beast
Say what the angel says the waters and the woman are in 17:15, 18
Say what 17:14 says about the Lamb

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon
nodes.d: An angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen, a voice calls God's people to come out of her, and kings, merchants and sailors mourn her sudden ruin while heaven is told to rejoice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happens to Babylon in Revelation 18 and who mourns?
ev: Say what the voice tells God's people in 18:4
Describe who mourns and why in 18:9-19
Say what heaven is told in 18:20

nodes.t: Hallelujah and the marriage supper of the Lamb
nodes.d: A great multitude in heaven praises God for judging the great whore, announces that the Lord God omnipotent reigns and that the marriage of the Lamb has come, and John is told that those called to the marriage supper are blessed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what is celebrated in heaven in Revelation 19:1-10?
ev: Say why the multitude rejoices in 19:1-2
Describe the bride and her clothing in 19:7-8
Say what the angel tells John when he falls to worship

nodes.t: The rider on the white horse and the defeat of the beast
nodes.d: Heaven opens and one called Faithful and True, The Word of God and King of kings, rides a white horse with a sharp sword from his mouth, and the beast and the false prophet are taken and cast into the lake of fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the rider on the white horse and what happens to the beast?
ev: Describe the rider and the names written on him
Say what happens to the beast and the false prophet

nodes.t: The binding of Satan and the thousand years
nodes.d: An angel binds the dragon, that old serpent, for a thousand years; John sees thrones and those who lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years, called the first resurrection, and the text says the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years ended.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Revelation 20:1-6 describes without adding more than the text says?
ev: Describe what happens to Satan in 20:1-3
Say what John sees about those on the thrones in 20:4-6
Say what is called the first resurrection

nodes.t: Satan loosed, the great white throne and the lake of fire
nodes.d: After the thousand years Satan is loosed and gathers Gog and Magog, fire from God devours them, the devil is cast into the lake of fire, and the dead are judged before a great white throne by their works, with death and hell cast into the lake of fire and those not in the book of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the great white throne judgment as Revelation 20:11-15 shows it?
ev: Describe what Satan does when loosed and what happens to him
Say what is judged and by what in 20:12-13
Say what is cast into the lake of fire in 20:14-15

nodes.t: A new heaven and a new earth
nodes.d: John sees a new heaven and new earth and the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God as a bride; God dwells with his people, wipes away every tear, and says he makes all things new, while the unbelieving have their part in the lake of fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God promises in Revelation 21:1-8?
ev: Say what the voice says about God dwelling with men
List what is gone in 21:4
Say what God says in 21:5-7

nodes.t: The holy city, new Jerusalem
nodes.d: An angel shows John the bride, the Lamb's wife, as a city with the glory of God, twelve gates named for the tribes of Israel and twelve foundations named for the apostles, no temple because God and the Lamb are its temple, and only those written in the Lamb's book of life entering.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the city John sees and what is said about its light and temple?
ev: Describe the walls, gates and foundations
Say why there is no temple and no need of sun
Say who enters according to 21:27

nodes.t: The river of life and the tree of life
nodes.d: John sees the river of the water of life from the throne of God and of the Lamb, with the tree of life on either side bearing twelve fruits and healing the nations, no more curse, and the servants seeing God's face and reigning for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Revelation 22:1-5 says is in the city?
ev: Describe the river and the tree
Say what 22:3 says about the curse
Say what God's servants do according to 22:3-5

nodes.t: Epilogue: I come quickly, the invitation and the warning
nodes.d: The angel and Jesus confirm the words are faithful and true, Jesus says he comes quickly with his reward and is the Alpha and Omega and the bright and morning star, the Spirit and the bride say Come and invite the thirsty, a warning is given about adding to or taking from the book, and the book ends with the grace of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Revelation ends and what invitation it gives?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself in 22:12-16
Quote the invitation of 22:17 in your own words
Say what the warning in 22:18-19 is about

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: The garden of Eden
nodes.d: God plants a garden, places the man in it with a command, and forms the woman as a helper fit for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the garden and the one thing God told the man not to do?
ev: Retell the formation of the man and the woman
State God's command about the tree (2:16-17)

nodes.t: The curse and the first promise
nodes.d: God pronounces judgment, yet promises that the woman's offspring will bruise the serpent's head (3:15), and clothes the man and woman before sending them from the garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the promise in Genesis 3:15?
ev: Name the consequences God gives in 3:14-19
Read 3:15 and say why it is called the first promise of a saviour

nodes.t: Jacob's blessing of Judah
nodes.d: Jacob blesses his sons, and says the sceptre shall not depart from Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jacob promised Judah in Genesis 49:10?
ev: Read 49:10 and identify to whom the blessing is addressed

nodes.t: The first plague: the river turned to blood
nodes.d: At the river's brink Moses and Aaron strike the water at the LORD's command; the river turns to blood, the fish die and the Egyptians cannot drink. The magicians do the same and Pharaoh's heart remains hard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the first plague and how Pharaoh responded?
ev: Say what God said Pharaoh would know by this sign (7:17)
Say what happened to the river and the fish (7:20-21)

nodes.t: Hear the statutes: no images, remember Horeb
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 4:1-40 urges Israel to keep the statutes without adding or taking away, to remember the day at Horeb when they heard the voice from the fire and saw no form, to make no image, to beware of forgetting the covenant, and warns of exile yet promises that the LORD, merciful, will be found when sought.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses told Israel to make no image of God?
ev: Say what Israel saw and did not see at Horeb and why that rules out images (4:12, 15-19).
Find the promise about seeking the LORD from exile (4:29-31).

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: The shoot from the stem of Jesse
nodes.d: A shoot from Jesse's stem, endowed with the Spirit of the LORD, judges the poor with righteousness; peace reaches even the animals, the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD, and the remnant is gathered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the one who comes from the stem of Jesse and the peace of his kingdom in Isaiah 11?
ev: List the gifts of the Spirit resting on him in Isaiah 11:2
Describe how he judges (11:3-5)
Describe the peaceful creation in 11:6-9 and the gathering in 11:10-12

nodes.t: Babylon's fall, Dumah and Arabia
nodes.d: Isaiah watches in fear at a grievous vision, the watchman announces that Babylon is fallen, Seir asks the watchman what remains of the night, and Arabia's glory is to fail within a year.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the watchman's report in Isaiah 21:6-9?
ev: Describe what the watchman reports in Isaiah 21:6-9
Say what the watchman answers in 21:11-12

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: New heavens and a new earth
nodes.d: The LORD answers a rebellious people, saves a remnant of his servants, and creates new heavens and a new earth and Jerusalem a joy where weeping is no more and the wolf and lamb feed together.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD says he will create in Isaiah 65:17-25?
ev: Say who the LORD preserves and who he judges (65:8-15)
Describe the new heavens and new earth (65:17-25)

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon and the return of Israel
nodes.d: The LORD declares through Jeremiah that Babylon will fall to a nation from the north, that Israel and Judah will return weeping and join themselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant, and that Babylon will be destroyed as Sodom was.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jeremiah 50-51 says will happen to Babylon and to Israel?
ev: Describe how Babylon falls (50:2-3, 51:30-32)
Describe the return of Israel and Judah (50:4-5, 19-20)
Say why the LORD judges Babylon (50:11, 24, 51:24)

nodes.t: Ezekiel's vision of the glory of the LORD
nodes.d: By the river Chebar Ezekiel sees a storm cloud with four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, a firmament, and above it a throne with a figure like a man in brightness; he falls on his face.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Ezekiel saw by the river Chebar and how he responded in Ezekiel 1:28?
ev: Describe the four living creatures and the wheels (1:5-21)
Describe the throne and what is on it (1:26-28)
Say how Ezekiel responds (1:28)

nodes.t: Daniel: overview
nodes.d: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, serve under Babylonian and Persian kings, and are delivered in the furnace and lions' den; Daniel interprets dreams and receives visions of kingdoms, the Ancient of days, and the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name Daniel and his three friends and say how the book of Daniel is arranged?
ev: Name Daniel and his three friends with their Babylonian names (1:6-7)
Say which kings Daniel served (1:21, 5:31, 6:28)
Describe the two halves of the book: stories (1-6) and visions (7-12)

nodes.t: Four beasts and the Ancient of days
nodes.d: In Belshazzar's first year Daniel dreams of four beasts rising from the sea, the last with ten horns and a boastful little horn; thrones are set, the Ancient of days sits in judgment, the beast is slain, and one like a son of man is given an everlasting kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the four beasts, the Ancient of days and the one like a son of man in Daniel 7:1-14?
ev: Describe the four beasts (7:3-8)
Describe the Ancient of days and the judgment (7:9-12)
Describe the one like the Son of man and what he is given (7:13-14)

nodes.t: The vision of the beasts interpreted
nodes.d: An attendant tells Daniel the four beasts are four kings, the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom for ever, and the little horn wars against the saints and speaks against the Most High until judgment is given and the kingdom is given to the saints.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Daniel is told the beasts are and what happens to the saints in Daniel 7:15-27?
ev: Say what the beasts and horns are told to be (7:17, 23-24)
Describe what the little horn does (7:21, 25)
Say what happens to the saints and the kingdom (7:18, 22, 26-27)

nodes.t: Michael stands up; many shall awake
nodes.d: Michael stands up in a time of trouble, those written in the book are delivered, many who sleep in the dust awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame, the wise shine like stars, and Daniel is told to seal the book until the time of the end and go his way to rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Daniel 12:2-3 says will happen to those who sleep in the dust and to the wise?
ev: Quote the promise in Daniel 12:2-3
Say what Daniel is told to do with the book (12:4, 9)
Report what Daniel is told for himself (12:13)

nodes.t: The lampstand and the two olive trees
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a gold lampstand with two olive trees; the LORD tells Zerubbabel that it is not by might nor power but by his spirit, that Zerubbabel who laid the foundation will finish the house, and that none should despise the day of small things.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Zerubbabel in Zechariah 4:6 and 4:9-10?
ev: Read 4:6 and say whom it is spoken to
Say what Zerubbabel's hands do (4:9)
Describe the two olive trees (4:14)
